pure-announcement.rationale: It is the project's standing docs index, not a launch, release note, or funding announcement, and the gateway-bridges-chat-apps-to-agents pattern it describes is not tied to a release event.

duplicate.rationale: The nearest concepts are all MCP governance and observability notes; none describe a self-hosted multi-channel messaging gateway for agents.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The claims are install commands, config keys, and architecture statements checkable against the MIT-licensed project itself.

durability.rationale: Most of the concrete content is release-sensitive setup detail — Node 26/22.22.3+/24.15+ support ranges, npm 11.16 flag differences, port 18789, the current channel roster — that will drift within months, leaving only a thin architecture sketch.

actionability.rationale: Its instructions are purely product operation (npm install -g openclaw, openclaw onboard, openclaw dashboard, allowFrom config), which helps someone run this tool but transfers no build-or-decide guidance beyond it.

atomicity.rationale: Despite the link-farm packaging, the page has exactly one stateable core — a single self-hosted gateway process is the source of truth bridging many chat channels to agent sessions — with everything else being navigation.
